text:
Mikael Granlund, 34 and wearing the Anaheim captaincy, has 26 points in 24 games and 13 in his last ten. The Hockey News called him "on pace to reach triple digit point total." That is a lovely headline for a player who has bounced through six NHL teams. Our numbers are more conservative, seeing him finish somewhere between 66 and 90.

The gap is luck. The Ducks have scored 8.3 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and at five on five they take just 40% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) when he plays, well below their rate without him. His plays-like comparisons all share the same note: chances against pile up with him on. He is still playing big minutes, 20:42 a night and climbing over the last ten, with 12 power-play points, and his own shooting is close to his normal range. Last season Evolving-Hockey had his team creating chances at a 90th percentile rate when he played. The question for Anaheim, losing lately and missing Leo Carlsson, is whether the captain's production holds once the bounces even out.
headline: Granlund's captaincy season is real, mostly
